title: check_array: dataframe input may already be a narwhals.DataFrame; read pandas-only attributes via to_native()
answers: check_array fails when passed a narwhals DataFrame
AttributeError 'sparse' or dtypes.apply in check_array with narwhals input
pandas sparse DataFrame wrapped in narwhals not converted to sparse matrix
how does check_array detect fully sparse pandas DataFrames
body:
Symptom: check_array raises an error when the input is a narwhals.DataFrame (e.g. one wrapping a pandas DataFrame, possibly with sparse columns) instead of a raw pandas DataFrame.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/validation.py:check_array called pandas-only API (`array.sparse`, `array.dtypes.apply`, `array.sparse.to_coo()`) directly on `array`, which may be a narwhals wrapper rather than the native frame.
Fix pattern: take the native object from the narwhals view (`df_pandas = array_df.to_native()`) and do all pandas-specific checks on it: SparseDtype detection, `dtypes_orig`, and the fully-sparse `df_pandas.sparse.to_coo()` conversion.
Constraints: any new pandas-specific logic in check_array's dataframe branch must use the native frame, not `array`. Callers may pass native or narwhals frames. check_array always returns a numpy array, Array API array, or scipy sparse array/matrix, never a dataframe. Test both forms by parametrizing with `nw.from_native(df)` (narwhals.stable.v2), as test_check_sparse_pandas_sp_format does.
